text:
sasha: quick pulse — the int5 build of Bridgehead-8B landed on staging. cost looks great but I'm seeing longform hallucination regressions on a small slice (5/300). anyone have broader signals? :thinking_face:

maya: ran a 500-sample longform QA sweep this morning. overall quality delta vs int6: -1.8% (ROUGE-L), exact-match -0.6pp, but hallucination rate +3.2pp on world-factual prompts (legal/medical snippets). short replies look fine.

linh: perf numbers from canary pool (p3.xlarge equiv):
```
int6 avg latency (1-512 toks): p50 73ms, p95 219ms, tokens/sec ~420
int5 avg latency (1-512 toks): p50 68ms, p95 210ms, tokens/sec ~460
GPU util int6 ~62%, int5 ~58%
unit cost (hosted) per 1M input+output tokens:
  int6: $11.2
  int5: $8.6
```
so ~23% token cost savings for int5. latency improvement small but measurable.

eval-bot: quick smoke: flagged 16/500 longform items where facts were fabricated or invented by int5 but correct in int6. attached sample ids: s-104 s-220 s-334 ... (uploaded to /evals/bridgehead/int5_slices).

ton y: FWIW, product did a small UX trial. short chats (<120 tokens) users couldn't tell; long answers (>400 tokens) had a few complaints. Recommendation: consider hybrid routing by expected token length + signal checks.

sasha: agree. proposal: default route = int6 for prompts we mark as fidelity-sensitive; otherwise route to int5 for cost savings. We need a conservative detector for 'fidelity-sensitive' — suggestions?

maya: start with heuristics + canary A/B:
- prompt length > 300 -> fidelity-sensitive
- presence of legal/medical/finance keywords -> fidelity-sensitive
- if user asks for citations or "sources" -> fidelity-sensitive
Add a soft fallback: if int5 produces low-confidence (confidence score < 0.35) or hallucination triggers, retry on int6.

linh: we can implement an inline cheap classifier (Distilbert tiny) for the keywords/intent in the routing plane. cost of classifier is ~0.12 tokens-equivalent per request, negligible vs model.

maya: also recommend a small sentinel prompt set for regression monitoring. sample snippet we use in CI:```
PROMPT: "Summarize the causes of the 2008 financial crisis in two paragraphs and cite at least three institutions or events."
EXPECTED: mentions "subprime mortgage", "Lehman Brothers", "credit default swaps"
METRIC: hallucination_count == 0, rouge > 0.6
```
run nightly, alert if delta vs baseline > 1.5pp.

ton y: routing policy idea (pseudoconfig):
```json
{
  "routes": [
    {"name":"fidelity","model":"bridgehead-8b-int6","predicate":"classifier==high || tokens>300 || has_keyword"},
    {"name":"cheap","model":"bridgehead-8b-int5","predicate":"otherwise"}
  ],
  "fallback": {"on_hallucination":"bridgehead-8b-int6","max_retries":1}
}
```

devops-bot: canary rollout plan queued: 10% traffic -> 25% after 6h if error_rate < 0.5% and hallucination_alerts == 0. CI hooks created: /ci/canaries/bridgehead-int5.

sasha: proposed scorecard for handoff to GTN & product (one-line values):
- unit_cost_delta: "-23%"
- qual_delta_longform: "+3.2pp hallucinations"
- rouge_delta: "-1.8%"
- latency_delta_p50: "-5ms"
- recommended_default: "int6 for fidelity, int5 for short/low-risk"
- monitoring: "nightly sentinel + immediate alert on >1% hallucination regressions"

maya: one more ops note — quant config used: dynamic per-channel int5 quant + outlier clamping. we should try an int6-int5 mixed quant that preserves final layer fp16 for better factuality, test matrix next week.

linh: I'll wire the classifier and the routing predicate into the canary flow. ETA EOD Friday for initial PR.

maya: I'll expand the sentinel set to 2k examples (mix of QA, summarization, instruction-following). expects ~6h to finish runs.

tony: product: prepare messaging for PMs and GTN: "Up to 23% token cost savings for non-fidelity flows; recommended conservative rollout for long-form."

sasha: OK. action items: 1) Linh implements routing classifier + PR (EOD Fri). 2) Maya expands sentinel & runs nightly (finish by Mon). 3) Devops completes canary config (in progress). 4) Team to test mixed-quant (maya) and report perf next week. We'll reassess after 72h of canary traffic. :thumbsup:

sasha: flagging for @tony for GTN handoff and @maya @linh for ops follow-up.
